articles.body: I made Coco, a small character for Claude Code. Coco lives in the little bar above the prompt, in both the terminal and the desktop app's Code tab. It's an unofficial fan mod, and it's free. The code uses the MIT license, and the art uses CC BY-NC 4.0. What does Coco do? Coco reacts to what Claude is doing: When Claude reads files, Coco's eyes follow the text. When Claude thinks, Coco makes a little bubble. When Claude writes code, Coco opens a thin black laptop and types too. When Claude finishes, Coco turns the screen around to show off. If there's an error, Coco jumps into a cardboard box. If Claude refuses, Coco puts a teapot lid on their head and sulks. Yes, HTTP 418. After 4 or 5 quiet minutes, Coco pulls down the hood and takes a nap.

articles.title: How TokenCap Eliminates Context Query Latency with Background Pre-Warming

articles.body: When integrating browser companions or IDE extensions with a local intelligence bridge, latency matters. If generating prompt context takes 4 or 5 seconds, developers stop using the integration. To deliver sub-second responses, TokenCap implements background cache pre-warming in src/bridge/warmCache.js . How Pre-Warming Operates When you run tokencap serve , the HTTP server begins listening immediately. While the pairing handshake occurs, an asynchronous worker kicks off: Graph Pre-Compilation: Traverses all files and loads AST symbol tables into memory. Memory and ADR Indexing: Loads active session records and architecture decisions into RAM. Git Diff Snapshotting: Caches uncommitted working tree diffs and affected symbols.

articles.title: ReconD: pull-based deployments for one server, without a platform
articles.excerpt: The simple use case is this: You have a machine And a containerized app running on that machine. Your CI pipeline already builds and publishes images. You do not want a full container orchestrator for…
articles.body: The simple use case is this: You have a machine And a containerized app running on that machine. Your CI pipeline already builds and publishes images. You do not want a full container orchestrator for this workload, but you also do not want to SSH into the box and manually run deploy scripts every time a new image is ready. That is the space reconD is designed for. reconD is a single-host deployment reconciliation agent. To put it simply, it watches your deployment metadata and deploys the latest version of your app. A typical workflow for a sample app called my-app Your CI publishes: a container image to GHCR a GitHub Release a deployment-metadata.json file that specifies the image, its immutable manifest digest, and the git SHA.

articles.title: How we made an Expo app feel native: Reanimated 4, real form sheets and haptics
articles.excerpt: An Expo app can feel native if every animation runs on the UI thread, every gesture hands its velocity to the spring that finishes it, and you use the system's own sheets instead of drawing your own.…
articles.body: An Expo app can feel native if every animation runs on the UI thread, every gesture hands its velocity to the spring that finishes it, and you use the system's own sheets instead of drawing your own. In 6pm that means Reanimated 4 worklets, Gesture Handler, Expo Router form sheets, and four kinds of haptic, each used for one job. 6pm is a daily money app. Its core moment, "the close", is a stack of receipt cards you swipe through at 6pm: right to keep, left to edit, down for "not mine". The last card stamps the day CLOSED. If that swipe feels like a web page, the product fails. So our agent contract (the CLAUDE.md at the repo root) opens with this: Native feel is the product. UI-thread animation only (Reanimated worklets, Gesture Handler).

articles.body: Apple revised the App Review Guidelines on October 16, 2026. Most of the changes are clarifications, but two are worth a minute if you ship iOS apps. What changed 2.5.19 (new number): hidden, dormant, or undocumented features. This used to sit inside 2.3.1. Now it is its own guideline and it names code obfuscation. The penalty can be removal and developer account termination. If a remote flag can turn on something the reviewer never saw, document it in Notes for Review or remove it from the binary. 2.3.14 (new): creative assets. The new creative assets that can appear in the product page header and search results follow normal metadata rules. No unverifiable claims ("#1", "best"), no misleading references to other apps, and no specific or discounted pricing. 1.2: user generated content.

articles.title: Proxies for AI agents: giving an agent reliable web access
articles.excerpt: Originally published on proxymint. Proxies for AI agents give a cloud-hosted agent a home or ISP origin. Which jobs need one, which type and rotation fit, and how to wire Playwright and MCP. An agent…
articles.body: Originally published on proxymint . Proxies for AI agents give a cloud-hosted agent a home or ISP origin. Which jobs need one, which type and rotation fit, and how to wire Playwright and MCP. TL;DR An agent on a cloud server browses from a hosting IP. Consumer sites that score networks read a datacenter ASN on the first request and often treat it as automated, so the exit type is chosen before the agent runs. The proxy type follows the agent's job. Agents that read APIs and docs need none or a flat-rate datacenter port, browser agents on consumer sites need residential, and recurring logged-in work needs a static ISP address. Rotation mode should follow the task, not the product default.

articles.title: Orionid meteor shower peaks tonight: Here's the best time to spot shooting stars
articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks tonight (Oct. 21-22) in the light of a waxing moon. Here's what to expect from one of Autumn's greatest natural light shows.
articles.body: Don't miss the Orionid meteor shower peak tonight (Oct. 21-22) as tiny shards of Halley's Comet collide with Earth's atmosphere to carve fiery streaks through the Autumn sky! But will the light cast by the waxing gibbous moon spoil the show? The Orionid meteor shower activity peaks when Earth travels through the densest section of the debris trail left by Comet 1P/Halley. The comet is currently racing back towards the sun ahead of its next visit to the inner solar system in 2061. Under perfect dark sky conditions 10 to 20 shooting stars could brighten the night sky each hour as the peak unfolds, according to NASA . However, the light cast by the waxing moon — just four days from being full — will likely reduce the number of visible meteors by hiding fainter Orionids from sight.
